correctness.rationale: The arcsine change of variable gives a uniform full-branch zigzag with g_q^n=g_(q^n). Each of the j whole branches contributes p/Q to the joint event. The partial branch contributes min(theta,p)/Q if increasing, and max(0,theta-(1-p))/Q if decreasing. Subtracting p^2 gives the claimed sign and minimum, with zeros exactly at integer Qp and maximum magnitude bounded by p(1-p)/Q. At a one-step grid threshold the two label indicators transfer to constants, so iteration factors all word probabilities. The full branch cylinders shrink and have equal weights q^(-m), giving entropy log q and the claimed strict information loss at q>=3. The q=2,p=1/4 counterexample gives lag one 1/16, lag two zero. Endpoints are null. Independent exact backward-branch checks (210 cases, replay: python3 /workspace/check_frozen_math.py) corroborate the covariance, not the infinite proof. Frozen verification notes and checker inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The threshold family is a natural observation of a full-branch chaotic map. The signed covariance with exact arithmetic zeros is a usable diagnostic: one adjacent-time covariance determines whether the entire observed process is Bernoulli, while isolated more distant zeros can be spurious. The all-lag formula and factor criterion add information beyond the known binary tent coding, exponential mixing bounds, or pairwise numerical tests.
